items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I had another fellow with me that was quite an arranger, and he was a pianist. He used to play piano sometimes on the things I'd direct

ctx.x: Right. Were -- you were doing most of the arranging for the band, or were you doing all of it? Was anybody else writing?

No. I had another fellow with me that was quite an arranger, and he was a pianist. He used to play piano sometimes on the things I'd direct, and he wrote for quartet, and he was quite a little arranger. Bob Crowder, my saxophonist, was an excellent little writer, and this particular arranger that I'm talking about, his name -- it's slipped my memory because this question came up -- but, Specks.

That's all I know him by, I can remember now, his name is Specks. Spencer was his first name, and he used to do a little writing for the Charioteers. He could write, and he was pretty thorough. Played very good piano, and he used to write some of the things for the show, and he had more time than I did, because he was more or less a handy man to the producer for the shows there which was Sammy Dye. And also, he would get paid extra when Sammy Dye would have rehearsals for the girls, you know, they had to have…
